small_guidance:
- The kernel is extremely slow (276ms) because each of B=128 programs loads the entire weight matrix W (32768×32768 fp32 = 4GB) on its own — total DRAM traffic is B×W = ~512GB. Increase K_SPLITS dramatically (e.g. 16-64) and also split N across programs so the grid is (B, N_tiles, K_tiles) — this lets many SMs share the weight loads via L2 reuse and parallelizes the work that currently serializes inside one program.
- Replace the scalar/row-vector accumulation pattern with a proper `tl.dot`-based GEMM tile: load X as a [BLOCK_M, BLOCK_K] tile across multiple batch rows (BLOCK_M=16 or 32, since B=128) so W tiles are reused across M. Currently each program does a matvec, getting zero W-reuse.
- Add autotune configs with BLOCK_M ∈ {16,32,64}, BLOCK_N ∈ {64,128}, BLOCK_K ∈ {32,64}, num_warps 4/8, num_stages 3/4, keyed on shapes.
large_guidance:
- Redesign as a tiled GEMM-then-reduce: program grid = (ceil(B/BLOCK_M), ceil(N/BLOCK_N)). Each program computes a [BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N] tile of (X @ W^T + b) with `tl.dot` accumulating over K in BLOCK_K chunks, then fuses pool+sum on the BLOCK_N axis (reshape to [BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N/2, 2], max over last dim, sum over middle) and atomic-adds the per-row partial scalar into out[b]. Final scale can be fused if only one N-tile per row, else a tiny scale kernel.
- Store W transposed once at init (shape [IN_FEATURES, OUT_FEATURES]) so the inner K-loop loads W contiguously along N — this is the standard GEMM layout and unlocks `tl.dot` efficiency on Ada.
- Consider a split-K strategy with atomics on out[b] given that K=32768 is large; combined with M-tiling this gives high SM occupancy (B=128 alone underfills 128 SMs once you also tile N).
